what: The machine-readable half of the P1-28 closing package. It names ONE commit as the phase's code candidate and records every measurement taken against it, with the provenance of each. docs/phase-1/phase-1-28/evidence/closure-evidence.md is the prose half and must state the same candidate; scripts/ci/build-p1-28-evidence-manifest.mjs refuses a disagreement between the two.
why: P1-27 shipped a closing page that pinned a head 47 commits behind the tree it described, and it went on reading like evidence because nothing compared the claim with the repository. A closing value that names no head is not a measurement of anything. Every figure below therefore carries the head it was taken at and the artefact it came from.
whatThisIsNot: This is not a tamper-proof seal and not a hosted observation. The digests in evidence-manifest.json remove SILENT revision, not revision. NO HOSTED FIGURE IN THIS PACKAGE WAS TAKEN AT THIS CANDIDATE. Every one of them comes from run 31750364479, which measured 38afa5c28e5b78d484a442cf6b8596fb2a5c34aa — a head three fix waves have since superseded — and each is recorded PENDING here, marked `describesSupersededHead`, and listed in `pendingHostedBindings`. What a later reader can do with them is fetch the same objects and see what that head did; what nobody may do with them is read them as a measurement of this candidate.

candidate.subject: chore(p1-28): regenerate the operation register and evidence seal after the finding fixes
candidate.whatFreezingMeans: Every LOCAL figure in this package describes THIS commit, or a named successor of it whose drift from it is declared path by path. Commits that land after it are documentation-and-machinery successors; each is required to leave apps/** and supabase/** byte-identical, so the product these measurements describe is the product at the candidate. A successor that changes either tree invalidates this package and the candidate must be re-frozen and re-measured — which is exactly what happened to the previous candidate and is recorded in `reFrozenFrom` below.
candidate.productIdentityExpectation: empty output — no product file differs between the candidate and any successor

reFrozenFrom.whyItWasRefused: Three finding-fix waves — `648fa46f` fix-product-honesty, `4eaf5d6a` fix-evidence-integrity, `3bd2298d` fix-record-accuracy, and the two fixes beneath them — changed 37 files under apps/** after that candidate was frozen. The seal COMPUTED `git diff --name-only 38afa5c2..HEAD -- apps supabase`, found it non-empty and refused the package, with five tests/ci cases red for that one reason. The refusal was correct: the package was describing software the branch no longer held.
reFrozenFrom.whatThisCostAndWhatItDidNot: The LOCAL tiers were re-measured here and are bound as usual. The HOSTED tiers could not be: a hosted run is taken by CI at a head, and this workstation cannot take one at all. Rather than carry the old head’s hosted figures forward as though they had been taken here, every hosted binding in this package is recorded PENDING at this candidate. See `pendingHostedBindings`.
reFrozenFrom.supersededSuccessorRecord: The previous candidate named three executable successors — `1b9811c8f489cd40b24dd1677add0f0dbfecfd7e` (the packaging commit), `897209637c43af8db7633d7e8b91a3766b0933cc` (the seal’s own test corrected) and `5e97dc9241179ca56d8aeb38599090072536e32d` (the seal bound to the repository). All three are ANCESTORS of this candidate, so they are no longer successors of anything and are not listed as such: `build-p1-28-evidence-manifest.mjs` refuses a recorded successor that is not in `git log <candidate>..HEAD`. They are kept here because deleting the record of what was once named would be the half-update the gate exists to catch.

candidate.vocabularyNote: `FINAL_CODE_SHA` and `FINAL_CODE_TREE` are the names this package was commissioned under and are used here so the commissioning brief and this record cannot drift apart. They are NOT the P1-27 spelling: that phase says `CODE_CANDIDATE_SHA` for the same idea, and no file in this repository used `FINAL_CODE_*` before this one. The mapping is recorded below rather than left for a reader to guess, because two names for one commit is exactly how a superseded head gets quoted as a current one.

vocabularyMapping.FINAL_CODE_SHA: P1-27 calls this CODE_CANDIDATE_SHA — the newest commit touching any non-document path.
vocabularyMapping.FINAL_CODE_TREE: The tree object of that commit. P1-27 records no equivalent field; it is added here because a tree id is what makes two checkouts comparable without trusting a commit message.
vocabularyMapping.EVIDENCE_RECORD_SHA: P1-27's name for the commit carrying the evidence file — here, each entry in `successors`.
vocabularyMapping.EXECUTABLE_DIFF_COUNT: P1-27's derivation `git diff --name-only CODE_CANDIDATE_SHA..EVIDENCE_RECORD_SHA` excluding docs/ and *.md. DOCUMENTATION_ONLY_RECORDING may be claimed only when it is exactly zero. This package does NOT claim DOCUMENTATION_ONLY_RECORDING for its first successor, and says so in `successors[0]`: that commit adds executable evidence machinery. It claims the narrower and checkable thing instead — that apps/** and supabase/** are byte-identical, so the PRODUCT measured is the product at the candidate.

successorRule: Every commit in `git log 6392ccb4..HEAD` that touches an EXECUTABLE path — anything outside `docs/` that is not `*.md` — must appear below by its full 40-character id, and `build-p1-28-evidence-manifest.mjs` computes the range and refuses an unnamed one. A DOCUMENTATION-ONLY successor may go unnamed, and the gate prints the ones that did: a commit cannot write its own id into a file it contains, so the rule "the list is exactly `git log`" is not one any repository can satisfy. That is the one hole, it is exactly one commit wide, and it is reported rather than hidden.

Three anchored claims are added pointing the other way, refusing a sentence that asserts an observation OF THIS CANDIDATE while the package records none. It also re-states run (6) in `.github/ci-baselines/unrun-test-tiers.json` as describing a superseded head. It adds no file under apps/** or supabase/** and changes none.

The first is the P1-27 failure this whole gate was written to prevent. A third state had to exist, and it had to demand MORE than silence rather than less.

successors.what: Seven cases in `tests/ci/p1-28-evidence-manifest.test.ts` that drive the PENDING and measurement-drift rules against THIS repository rather than against a synthetic one, and three existing cases moved with the rules: the tier-provenance case accepts either local provenance while requiring the ledger reconciliation unchanged; the hosted-attestation case requires headSha === candidate for a tier that CLAIMS an observation here and requires a PENDING tier to declare which head its figures belong to; and the anchored-claim case is split so that a denial is refused while a run IS bound and allowed while none is.

successors.kind: evidence machinery — the hosted circularity removed, and the merge-ref false positive with it
successors.what: Two corrections to the seal. HOSTED: a binding may cite a run taken at a head that is NOT the candidate provided it declares `describesProductIdenticalSuccessor` and the gate COMPUTES all of — that head is a commit this repository contains, it DESCENDS from the candidate, `git diff --name-only <candidate>..<runHead> -- apps supabase` is EMPTY (a diff git refuses to take is UNKNOWN, never empty), and `headSha` names that head so a reader sees which commit was exercised. An ancestor head is refused by it and stays on the `describesSupersededHead` path, and a binding may not wear both markers. SUCCESSORS: the set is what THIS BRANCH added after the freeze, computed in two independent subtractions — the base branch is resolved to a commit and excluded from the range, and a checkout that is a synthetic merge of this branch with its base is judged as the branch side of that merge, but only when the merge carries no content of its own. Both fail closed: a base this checkout cannot resolve makes the successor set UNKNOWN and is refused. It adds eleven known-bad worlds and twelve tree-level cases; it adds no file under apps/** or supabase/** and changes none.
successors.why: TWO defects, both of which made the gate say something false about itself. (1) A hosted binding cleared only when its headSha WAS the candidate — and the seal's own machinery cannot live inside the commit it seals, so hosted CI necessarily runs at a later head. Every hosted run therefore forced another re-freeze whose seal commit moved the head again, without end. (2) `actions/checkout` defaults for a pull_request to the MERGE REF, so `git log <candidate>..HEAD` swept in the base branch's own history: hosted CI reported 0c89647de1a661105ec3a612955789989da58a0d — a develop commit authored by another session, absent from this branch — as an unnamed executable successor of this candidate, and the same ref would have made the product-identity diff report the base's changes as a broken freeze.
successors.provedByFailingFirst: Nine mutations of the seal, applied one at a time and each observed red before being reverted: the descent check, the product-identity check, the containment check, the refused-diff check, the undeclared-head check, the base subtraction, the merge-ref unwrap, the fail-closed base, and the evil-merge guard. Every one of the fifty-six known-bad worlds and seven tree-level cases that stood before this commit still fails.
successors.measurementHead: This is the head both LOCAL tiers were measured at. A tier run before it would report a suite that does not include its twelve cases. The three executable paths that differ between it and the candidate are what both tiers declare as `measurementDrift`.

howTierFiguresAreChecked: Four obligations, because there are four kinds of claim. ARITHMETIC: `passed + failed + skipped` must equal the declared total, for every tier — the review set `passed: 3, failed: 812` beside `tests: 2475` and the first revision of the gate accepted it, because nothing added the three numbers up. LOCAL: the figures must equal the P1-27 run ledger’s, read out of git at the commit named in `localLedger.atCommit`, and a LOCAL tier may carry no figure the ledger does not write. MEASUREMENT HEAD: the head a local tier names must be executable-identical to the candidate, or a NAMED successor of it carrying no product drift and declaring `measurementDrift` exactly equal to what `git diff --name-only <head>..<candidate>` computes. HOSTED: cannot be computed from this repository at all, and the gate says so in those words; what it requires instead is that the claim be FETCHABLE — a run id, a job id, the head the job ran at, and the artefact — and, when that head is not the candidate, that the record SAY WHICH OF TWO THINGS IT IS — a head the candidate SUPERSEDES, marked `describesSupersededHead`, proved an ancestor and listed in `pendingHostedBindings`; or a head that DESCENDS from the candidate, marked `describesProductIdenticalSuccessor`, whose apps/** and supabase/** `git diff` computes to be identical to the candidate's. Either way the head must be a commit this repository contains.

P1-28-OD-001.title: who administers the intake catalogues, and through which surface
P1-28-OD-001.whatMustBeDecided: (a) WHO administers the intake catalogues — a tenant administrator, a head-office role, or the platform operator; and (b) THROUGH WHICH SURFACE — a screen inside this product, a separate administration application, or provisioning performed outside the product altogether.
P1-28-OD-001.consequenceToday: Seven intake catalogues ship zero rows and no screen in this product can add one. Two of those tables sit on a REQUIRED foreign key of an operator path — appointmentTypeId on apt.appointment-create and cancellationReasonId on apt.appointment-cancel — so until a catalogue is populated no appointment can be booked and none can be cancelled.

PR #227 registered 21 catalogue-management writes behind apt.catalogue.manage / rec.catalogue.manage; no seed grants either code to any role, so the capability is held by nobody. All 21 are recorded DELIBERATELY_ABSENT against this decision in docs/phase-1/phase-1-28/write-reachability.json, and check-p1-28-write-reachability.mjs resolves that reference against the §7 headings, so the classification cannot be entered with a fabricated decision id.

ownerAcceptance.rule: The permanent Frontend closure rule from P1-26 onward: no Frontend phase closes without the Product Owner testing the running application in real installed Chrome and returning `OWNER ACCEPTANCE: PASS` verbatim. Silence is never Pass. Automated CI is necessary and is not sufficient.
ownerAcceptance.howToRun: npm run acceptance:serve — a production build, never dev:all. A dev stack compiles route bundles lazily and the API authenticator is installed as a side effect of composing the IAM module, so an acceptance session on a dev stack reports product defects that do not exist.
ownerAcceptance.note: This package is the technical evidence an acceptance session rests on. It is NOT a closure record and does not close the phase. IT IS ALSO NOT YET THE COMPLETE TECHNICAL EVIDENCE: eleven hosted bindings are PENDING at this candidate (see `pendingHostedBindings`). An acceptance session may be run against this build at any time, but the automated half of the case is not finished until the coordinator’s exact-head run binds them.

pendingHostedBindings.what: Every binding in this package that describes a head other than the candidate, listed by name. The gate DERIVES this set from the documents’ own `headSha` fields and refuses a difference in either direction, so a pending binding cannot go unlisted and a listed one cannot be decorative.
pendingHostedBindings.awaits: an exact-head CI run at the candidate 6392ccb4321b004ed12e5d04ad583298da3303dd, taken by the phase coordinator
pendingHostedBindings.whyNoneCanBeTakenHere: A hosted figure is produced by a GitHub-hosted runner. This workstation can run the unit and web tiers and nothing else in this list: the backend and database tiers need a running PostgreSQL it does not host, the browser tier needs the full acceptance stack, and hosted CI, CodeQL, the dependency audit and the production build are properties of a RUN, not of a checkout.
pendingHostedBindings.whatTheCoordinatorMustDo: Run CI and bind the real figures. A binding leaves the pending state in exactly two ways and must declare which: (1) its `headSha` IS the candidate 6392ccb4321b004ed12e5d04ad583298da3303dd; or (2) its `headSha` is a commit this repository CONTAINS, which DESCENDS from the candidate, whose apps/** and supabase/** the gate COMPUTES to be byte-identical to the candidate's, and which the binding marks `describesProductIdenticalSuccessor`. The second exists because the seal's own machinery cannot live inside the commit it seals, so hosted CI necessarily runs at a later head; under the old rule every hosted run forced another re-freeze whose seal commit moved the head again. What is still refused is a run at a head the candidate SUPERSEDES (that stays `describesSupersededHead`, and stays pending), a run at a head this repository does not contain, and a run at a descendant whose product differs — in which case the candidate must be re-frozen there and the local tiers re-measured, exactly as this cycle did.
